messages.subject: error when using non-stationary setting
parts:
Hi help,
 
I can do stationary modelling well just using
spde1 <- inla.spde2.matern(mesh,alpha=2)

I tried to use non-stationary models, so I did like this,
  Btau <- cbind(0,1,0,mesh$loc[,1],0)
  Bkappa <- cbind(0,0,1,0,0)
  spde1 <- inla.spde2.matern(mesh,alpha=2,B.tau=Btau,B.kappa=Bkappa,theta.prior.mean=rep(0,4),theta.prior.prec=rep(1,4))

saying tau is a linear function of mesh$loc[,1], and kappa is a constant.
However, when I call inla, it has an error. .

        GMRFLib version 3.0-0-snapshot, has recived error no [12]
        Reason    : The Newton-Raphson optimizer did not converge
        Message   : Condition `lambda < 1.0 / lambda_lim' is not TRUE

What's the problem here ?

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] error when using non-stationary setting
parts:
On 21 Jan 2014, at 17:41, Liu David <xyli...@gmail.com> wrote:
I tried to use non-stationary models, so I did like this,
  Btau <- cbind(0,1,0,mesh$loc[,1],0)
  Bkappa <- cbind(0,0,1,0,0)

That gives you four parameters, but the fourth parameter will have no influence over the model.
Delete the final ",0" on both lines, so that you only have three parameters, and see if that removes the later error. (Adjust the 4s to 3s where needed)

Finn L

spde1 <- inla.spde2.matern(mesh,alpha=2,B.tau=Btau,B.kappa=Bkappa,theta.prior.mean=rep(0,4),theta.prior.prec=rep(1,4))

saying tau is a linear function of mesh$loc[,1], and kappa is a constant.
